scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating high-index/low-index dielectric stack with individually optimized thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high reflectance in the 300-450 nm band and high transmittance in the 1000-1700 nm band on fused silica substrate at normal incidence.
expected_advantages: 24 layers provide sufficient design freedom for dual-band optimization
Alternating sequence is manufacturable with standard deposition tools
Individual thickness optimization allows finer spectral control than periodic stacks
Fused silica substrate transmits well in both target bands
known_risks: Uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal vs. fewer layers with better thickness distribution; would need comparison runs to settle
Uncertain exact refractive index dispersion of hfo2 and sio2 in the 300-1700 nm range from memory; actual values come from material catalog datasets
Uncertain whether alternating sequence starting with HfO2 is superior to starting with SiO2 for this specific band combination; this is a hypothesis
The ±10% initialization variance around prior best may constrain search if the prior solution is in a local optimum; would need to verify improvement over full random seeding
Recalled quarter-wave rule is approximate; actual optimal thicknesses may deviate significantly from λ/4n predictions
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise or remain stable compared to iteration-08 value of 0.7999 if the refined search is effective
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if solutions remain physically valid
valid_candidates count should remain high (≥5) indicating the search space is well-bounded
thicknesses_nm values should show reduced variance compared to full random seeding, clustering near the iteration-08 best solution
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 10 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.5 for three consecutive rounds, reduce mutation step-size by another 25% and continue
